Jess (eng-runtime): Quick ask — can someone run a power/thermal comparison across A100 / H100 / L40S for the 20B transformer (seq=2048)? Want perf-per-watt numbers, any thermal throttling incidents, and steady-state behavior. Target batches: 1, 4, 16. Please upload raw CSVs + a 1-line summary to s3://redwood-bench/thermal/1832102023.

Omar A.: I can take A100 + L40S tomorrow in lab-2. H100 is queued for me today but might free up Thu. Do we want a specific driver/CUDA stack pinned? Also: should I test with and without power caps?

Laura M.: I can run H100 on Thu. Our last good baseline used CUDA 12.2 + driver 535 + NCCL 2.17 — recommend that stack for comparability. Yes to powercap tests. For consistency, avoid MIG on A100 for these runs (full-card only). Sample commands I'm using: 
```
# perf runner (example)
python bench/run_infer.py --model redwood-20b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --samples 200 --out /tmp/run.csv

# power monitoring (1s sample)
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,power.draw --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/power.csv
```

Kai T.: Couple of measurement notes: keep a 30s warmup (ignore first 30s of samples) for steady-state; capture p50/p90/p99 latencies and tokens/sec. Compute perf-per-watt as (tokens/sec) / (avg power.draw). Label each run with: sku, driver, powercap (none/250/300/350), batch. Also include GPU clock & mem clock in logs.

Jess (eng-runtime): Naming convention: s3://redwood-bench/thermal/1832102023/{sku}/{driver}/{powercap}/{batch}/run-<timestamp>.csv and place a README.txt in each folder with env + runner args. When you upload, paste a 1-line summary here e.g. "A100: batch4 uncapped -> 18k tok/s @ 310W avg -> 58 tok/s/W; no throttling". @Omar A. @Laura M. :raised_hands:

benchbot: Lab reservation created — A100 (lab-2) 2026-03-19 09:00 UTC; H100 (lab-3) 2026-03-19 14:00 UTC.

Omar A.: I'll run A100 and L40S. Planning powercap sweep: none, 250W, 300W. Will also log GPU temps and clocks. Expect initial CSVs by EOD Thu and a short paste here.

Laura M.: H100 booked Thu 14:00 UTC. I'll run uncapped + capped 350W. Using CUDA12.2/535. Will upload run CSVs + power.csv and a small readme.

Kai T.: If you hit sustained temps >85C during steady-state, note the GPU clock curve and include dmesg/syslog lines — that usually indicates thermal limits or driver throttles. Also test with a small single-core pinned run to check cooling baseline if suspicious.

Jess (eng-runtime): Awesome — thank you. If any of you want me to tweak the bench runner (warmup/window sizes or csv schema) I can push a tiny patch. Quick sync penciled for Fri 2026-03-20 10:30 UTC to compare numbers unless someone posts earlier.

Omar A.: Copy — will post preliminary numbers here.

Laura M.: Will do.

Kai T.: Thanks all, I'll prepare an analysis notebook template to compute tok/s/W and p99 deltas and drop it into the s3 path so everyone can run it locally.

Jess (eng-runtime): Perfect — tagging this done for coordination. Ping if blockers come up.
